messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance SLOs & Autoscaling follow-up / FlowMetrics

Hi Carlos / FlowMetrics eng team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can line up the M A P:

Summary of requirements from our discussion:
- Latency SLO: target 95th percentile end-to-end for streaming responses (token-to-token and final response). You mentioned wanting <200ms ideally; want to confirm precise target.
- Throughput / concurrency: stated peak concurrent streams ~180 with average baseline ~50; bursts up to ~500 for promotions.
- Streaming: token-level streaming required (client expects partial tokens as they arrive).
- Autoscaling/burst: ability to absorb 3-5 minute bursts; require warm pool or pre-warmed capacity to bring concurrency to burst levels with minimal cold-start latency.
- Failure/queueing behavior: prefer graceful degradation (throttling/queueing) rather than request failures; we discussed queue thresholds and retry windows.

Actions / clarifying Qs for you:
1) Can you confirm your target 95th latency SLO (ms) for streaming? Is 150ms / 200ms / 250ms realistic?
2) For bursts, what’s the typical ramp profile — e.g., 10x traffic in 30s, sustained for 2–5 minutes?
3) Any constraints on cold-start time for you (acceptable scale-up window)?
4) Are there any authentication / routing constraints (VPC, private endpoints) we should plan for in the MAP?

Attachments: SLO_QA_Template.pdf (SLO questionnaire) and a draft mutual_action_plan.xlsx for timeline/owners.

Next steps: if you can reply with the three clarifications above, we’ll draft two autoscale policies (conservative and aggressive) plus a recommended warm-pool config and share a short PRFAQ for the SLO evaluation.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscaling follow-up / FlowMetrics

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers inline below.

> 1) Can you confirm your target 95th latency SLO (ms) for streaming?
We currently aim for 95th <= 200ms for interactive features; for batch generation it's laxer. For streaming chat we’d prefer <=150ms if feasible, but 200ms is acceptable as a fall-back.

> 2) For bursts, what’s the typical ramp profile?
We see 5–10x ramps in ~30–60s triggered by marketing pushes. Bursts usually last 2–6 minutes (short campaigns). Peak concurrency observed: 500 concurrent streams during last campaign; baseline mid-day 120–200 concurrent.

> 3) Any constraints on cold-start time?
We need <60s to be at near-peak capacity for hard bursts; <30s ideal. Prefer warm pool approach so steady-state latency is not affected.

> 4) Any auth/routing constraints?
We use standard OAuth tokens; would like private endpoint (VPC) for production. We can share network/contact details via secure doc.

One more note: streaming is required for the front-end feature (progressive rendering). If streaming degrades, front-end falls back to polling which is suboptimal.

Happy to jump on another 30-min call next week to review the MAP.

—Carlos
Carlos Mendes
Head of Platform | FlowMetrics
carlos@flowmetrics.com

Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscaling follow-up / FlowMetrics (internal)

Marissa / Rachel —

Thanks for sharing the notes and Carlos’ quick answers. A few engineering notes we should propose back to FlowMetrics (short and pragmatic):

1) Warm pool and pre-warmed instances– Suggest recommending a warm pool sized to cover expected burst headroom. From Carlos’ numbers: baseline 200, peak 500 -> warm pool 250 instances (or equivalent capacity) to cover 300 concurrent rise without cold starts. We can present both instance-count and vGPU-equivalent options.

2) Scale-up timeline– Our runtime supports pre-warmed instances that can be immediately assigned; for capacity beyond warm pool we rely on autoscaler (spot/on-demand) which typically ramps in ~45–90s depending on cloud region. We should advertise conservative SLA: reach 80% of burst target within 45s given warm pool + fast routing; full burst capacity within 90s.

3) Queueing/Throttling policy– Recommend a queue threshold at ~80% of per-instance concurrency. When queueing is active we can return a preflight header to clients indicating delay, and expose a retry-after. Prefer queue to hard failures.

4) Streaming considerations– For token-level streaming we need to ensure KV cache warm-up and pinning for long-lived streams; recommend sticky routing for active streams and keepalive pings.

5) Monitoring + SLO evaluation– Propose instrumenting 95th/99th token latency, cold-start counts, warm-pool utilization, and queue length. We'll include alert thresholds and an SLO dashboard in Redwood Console.

Action: I'll update mutual_action_plan.xlsx with two autoscale policy proposals (conservative/aggressive) and an estimated cost delta for warm pool sizes. Marissa — can you send to Carlos with recommended SLO text and proposed next-call times?

Thanks,
Dev Patel

Hi Carlos —

Appreciate the quick clarifications — this is super helpful. Based on the numbers and our internal options, here are the proposed commitments and next steps so we can lock the MAP: 

Proposed SLO / autoscale summary:
- SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end token latency <= 150ms (goal). Fall-back SLO 95th <= 200ms acceptable for the first 30 days after cutover while we tune.
- Warm pool: propose pre-warmed capacity to cover +300 concurrent on top of baseline (we’ll present instance or vGPU-equivalent options). For your 500 peak we’d size warm pool to handle ~300 of the delta, with autoscale covering the rest.
- Scale-up: expected reach of ~80% of burst target within 45s (warm pool + routing), full capacity within 90s.
- Queueing: prefer queueing over hard failures. Recommend queue when utilization >80% per-instance and expose retry-after headers. We’ll tune thresholds in the canary.
- Streaming: we’ll enable sticky routing for long-lived streams and ensure KV-cache pinning to avoid token-level cold starts.

Next steps / timeline:
1) We’ll send an updated MAP (attached) with owners and dates — please review and mark any redlines.
2) Proposed 30-min follow-up next Tue or Wed to review policies and select NPIs (network/private endpoint).
3) We'll run a short pre-cutover canary (2–4 hours) to validate 95th latency with warm pool and autoscale enabled.

Links: HubSpot deal — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/421
SLO template — https://docs.redwood.com/shared/slo-template

If this looks good, would you confirm the 95th target (150ms goal / 200ms fallback) and availability for a call next week?

Best,
